summary: Measured webpack 4.44.2's actual decode from the holdout's committed baseline chunk: UTF-8 with U+FFFD replacement, not latin1 — proven by the valid-UTF-8 sibling module carrying the same names through the same toolchain with accents intact. Implemented the byte-keyed capability (encoding classification, invalid-byte offsets, webpack's utf8BufferToString, pre-load plugin scoped to dependency JS) and led the composed CRA adapter with it. Valid UTF-8 returns null so those files stay untouched; UTF-16/32 refuse truthfully. Added fixture-scale red/green vite builds, negatives, a React overfitting guard, a self-verifying evidence record cross-checked against the immutable holdout receipt. tsc, lint, and 1289 node tests green.

summary: The memos session gate cannot be opened by the application's own sign-in flow, so no behind-the-gate journey can be written truthfully. Signin.tsx validates email AND password with maxLength 24 before calling api.login; the frozen seed's owner email is 34 chars and MEMOS_OWNER_PASSWORD is 26, so both are refused client-side and login is never issued. Signup is unreachable because the seed holds an OWNER, so /api/status reports one and the button renders 'Sign in'. All four required journeys live behind that gate. Fixing it requires changing the frozen seed, which moves the 1672b43f behavior digest — a drift the packet forbids. No files written.
open_questions: Should the frozen projection seed be amended so the owner credential pair passes the pinned client's own validator (minLength 4, maxLength 24, noSpace) — e.g. email 'owner@evidence.invalid' (22 chars) and MEMOS_OWNER_PASSWORD 'synthetic-pass' (14 chars)? This necessarily moves seedSha256, MEMOS_PROJECTION_BEHAVIOR_DIGEST off 1672b43f, and the projection block of evidence/runs/react-memos-v0-1-3/t006-api-surface.json.

If the seed must stay frozen, is there a sanctioned alternative for opening the gate that is still the application's own flow? I found none: appRouter has only /signin and *->Home, Home gates unconditionally on GET /api/user/me, POST /api/user needs a prior session, and profile.mode 'prod' means the dev prefill (demo@usememos.com/secret) never fires and would 401 regardless.

Should u12 be re-cut as two units — one amending the seed and re-freezing the digest plus the enumeration record, then one witnessing the journeys — given the digest change also touches the u11 enumeration facts?

summary: Read-only Angular cohort-two scout. Fixed the graveyard from t005/t011 plus the retired spine board, then harvested 646 repos still carrying .angular-cli.json and star-ranked them via GraphQL, proving no production app survives at HEAD in that format. Delivered a 5-candidate ranked shortlist with LICENSE blob sha+size+copyright verified at each exact pin, ~30 rejects with reasons, and a 2-cell cut: altair v1.9.0 (Angular 5/CLI 1.6, .angular-cli.json) then super-productivity v2.13.15 (Angular 8 pre-Ivy, zero backend), with tiny-translator v0.12.0 as the C1 swap and pigallery2 1.7.0 as the un-ingested holdout reserve. Two rulings owed: altair's placeholder copyright, super-productivity's git-protocol dependency.

summary: Calibration found a real cross-lane behavioral break, so nothing was published. Migrated (Angular 16.2) silently discards a typed translation: textarea.ng-dirty set in both lanes, but app-normalized-message-input stays ng-pristine, undo never enables (>11s) and the exported XLIFF carries state=final with the ORIGINAL text; baseline (Angular 5) propagates within ~200ms. App source is a faithful .debounceTime->.pipe(debounceTime) translation, so this is a runtime regression invisible to both build lanes. Landed real measured journey corrections (filter-label selectors, reviewer-half semantics, download settle, debounce anchor); tsc and lint clean.
open_questions: Migrated lane loses typed translations: the component's debounced form.valueChanges -> propagateChange never reaches the outer formControlName control under Angular 16.2, while the era lane fires it in ~200ms. Is this repaired by a migration capability (outside this unit's contract) or published as a recorded behavioral difference? Publishing this vertical green is impossible until that is decided.

The RED record under evidence/runs/angular-tiny-translator-v0-12-0/ was not written (wall clock). Re-cut a small unit to drive both lanes through a u19d-style record driver; the discriminator is mechanical: the journey's settled-state wait on '#translation button[mat-icon-button]' losing 'disabled' passes on baseline and times out on migrated.

Second, still-uncalibrated divergence: the baseline lane clears the editor-commit wait then fails at 'All units' with expected 3 / observed 2 (the untranslated count), suggesting the TranslationFileView is reconstructed after the reviewer commit. Needs one baseline calibration pass with stage-labelled probes.

Core schema amendments (observerFinalization.workerEvents, refusedServiceWorker shape, recorded-amendment list, core receipt test updates) were not attempted, since they should follow a settled journey.

effortJustification: Silent data loss across an eleven-major migration whose source was translated by our own capability — the root cause decides whether an adapter transform is defective, and a wrong attribution here corrupts both the capability and the evidence corpus.

summary: Reconnaissance complete; no files written. Two findings. (1) Blocking: u18-era-baseline.json's 64-entry inventory publishes sha256(readFileSync(path,'latin1')), not sha256 of the files — 64/64 match latin1, only 22/64 match real sha256. Same defect in three published angular-factoriolab records. The era lane cannot be bound as goal item 1 requires, since the witness verifier computes real sha256 over the served root. Retained rebuild-*.manifest.txt files are raw-correct and offer a clean rebinding. (2) The font-inlining probe found an undeclared, migration-introduced, every-build fetch to fonts.googleapis.com against a consent that sets alternateHostsAllowed:false.
open_questions: Era-lane binding: bind the served era root to the raw-correct retained rebuild-2/rebuild-3.manifest.txt and issue a supersede-by-reference correction record under evidence/runs/angular-super-productivity-v2-13-15/, or re-issue the inventory with raw digests as a new u18k record? Both change what u20b/u20c bind to, so I want the ruling before writing the schema.

The latin1 digest defect also sits in evidence/runs/angular-factoriolab/{m2-era-baseline,m2-migrated-build,m2-build-parity}.json, which back a PUBLISHED vertical and are outside my file contract. Comparison conclusions stay valid (latin1 decoding is byte-injective); only the published digest values are wrong. Who owns that correction, and should the digest-writing harness be fixed centrally first?

Font locality: fonts.googleapis.com is on no allowlist (consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 declares alternateHostsAllowed:false; allowed hosts are registry.yarnpkg.com, registry.npmjs.org, codeload.github.com, github.com), and a production build is neither acquisition nor a package-manager window. Does this need a consent amendment or a rebuild with optimization.fonts.inline disabled before the witness vertical publishes?
Published angular-tiny-translator asserts the same Angular 16 build-time Google Fonts inlining, so it likely carries the same undeclared fetch. Should that be probed as a separate unit?

summary: Root cause proven from both bundles + Angular 16 runtime: Ivy fires input setters in template order (splitPos before splitTopEl) whereas Angular 8 View Engine applied them in directive-declaration order (splitTopEl[0] before splitPos[5]); set splitPos dereferences the not-yet-populated this.splitTopEl -> classList error. App-latent assumption (b) exposed by genuine Ivy ordering change (a); template and component are byte-identical to source (not c). But Angular 16 ships NO vendor mechanism/provider/config to restore VE input ordering, so the packet's prescribed fix shape (vendor-guarded, app-source-unchanged) is unrealizable; the only working generic fix reorders authored template bindings, violating 'App source stays as its authors wrote it'. Made no file changes.
open_questions: No Angular provider/config/compiler-flag exists to reorder Ivy input-setter invocation (verified in core.mjs 16.2.12). Which constraint should be relaxed?
